notes: Read the complete poverty target, preceding U.S. poverty context, all twelve candidates and the review. Preserved can rather than upgrading the ten-year poverty reduction to a guaranteed commitment; restored U.S. scope for children; restored the productivity-sharing rationale to the EITC and minimum-wage proposals; split the fair-pay, mothers and responsible-fatherhood positions and the business, housing and promise-neighborhood positions; and separated the proposed neighborhood design from the descriptive Harlem Children's Zone example.

claims.claim_text: Working together, the United States can cut poverty in half within ten years.
Commitment to provide every child in the United States a world-class education from early childhood through college.
Commitment to expand the Earned Income Tax Credit so workers share in U.S. productivity.
Commitment to raise the minimum wage and index it to inflation so workers share in U.S. productivity.
Commitment to work for fair pay to combat poverty, given that most adults in poverty are women.
Commitment to support mothers to combat poverty, given that most adults in poverty are women.
Commitment to policies promoting responsible fatherhood to combat poverty, given that most adults in poverty are women.
Commitment to bring businesses back to U.S. inner cities.
Commitment to increase the U.S. supply of affordable housing.
Commitment to establish promise neighborhoods providing comprehensive services in areas of concentrated poverty and based on proven models.

The Harlem Children's Zone in New York City seeks to engage all residents around goals including parenting-school attendance, meaningful-employment retention, college for every participating student, and strong child physical and mental health outcomes.
